---
title: "Food supply, socioeconomic drivers and obesity in Sub-Saharan Africa"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
if (!exists("DATA_DIR")) DATA_DIR <- "data"      # folder with the input files (see README)
if (!exists("FIG_DIR"))  FIG_DIR  <- "figures"   # folder where PNG figures are saved
dir.create(FIG_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# OVERVIEW OF THIS ANALYSIS
# 1. Food supply (FAO Food Balance Sheets): two releases (1990-2013, 2010-2022) are cleaned, grouped into
#    food groups and harmonised into one 1990-2022 series.
# 2. Socioeconomic drivers (World Bank-style indicators + GNI) are cleaned and merged.
# 3. Obesity prevalence (NCD-RisC) is cleaned and averaged over sexes.
# 4. Trend plots (SSA average vs Kenya vs World) and comparison with EAT-Lancet reference ranges.
# 5. Spearman correlations with obesity, then fuzzy-set QCA (fsQCA) for 1992 and 2022:
#    necessity analysis, truth tables, complex / parsimonious / intermediate solutions, sensitivity checks.
```

# Food supply data
```{r}
#Load dataset 1990-2013
# ---- 1. FOOD SUPPLY: HISTORIC FAO FOOD BALANCE SHEETS (1990-2013) ----
# Reads the historic FAOSTAT file (wide format: one column per year).
# Steps: reshape to long -> drop missing/flag values -> keep SSA countries,
# selected elements and food items -> convert units -> aggregate into food groups.
all_data1 <- read_excel(file.path(DATA_DIR, "FoodBalanceSheetsHistoric_E_All_Data.xlsx"))
View(all_data1)
#######################
#clean data
# Wide -> long: one row per Area/Item/Element/Year.
all_data <- all_data1 %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("Y19") | starts_with("Y20"), names_to = "Year", values_to = "Value")

print(all_data)
View(all_data)
#######################
# Remove rows where Value is "X"
all_data <- all_data %>%
# "X" marks missing values in the FAO file, so those rows are removed.
  filter(Value != "X")

print(all_data)
#######################
#Remove "Y" from Year column
all_data <- all_data %>%
  mutate(Year = str_remove(Year, "^Y"))

print(all_data)
#######################
# Remove unnecessary columns
colnames(all_data)
# Drop FAO code columns that are not needed (names/labels are kept instead).
columns_to_remove <- c("Area Code (M49)", "Area Code", "Item Code", "Item Code (FBS)", "Element Code", "1961", "19612")
all_data <- all_data %>% select(-all_of(columns_to_remove))

print(all_data)
#######################
#Rename Area to Region
# "Region" is the common key used to join with the drivers and obesity data.
names(all_data)[names(all_data) == "Area"] <- "Region"

print(all_data)
unique(all_data$Item)
unique(all_data$Element)
unique(all_data$Region)
#######################
#select countries
# Countries analysed: 38 Sub-Saharan African (SSA) countries plus "World" for comparison.
# Names follow FAO spelling here and are harmonised to World Bank spelling just below.
regions_to_keep <- c(
  "Angola", "Benin", "Botswana", "Burkina Faso", "Cabo Verde", "Cameroon",
  "Central African Republic", "Chad", "Congo", "Côte d'Ivoire",
  "Eswatini", "Ethiopia", "Gabon", "Gambia", "Sao Tome and Principe",
  "Ghana", "Guinea", "Guinea-Bissau", "Kenya", "Lesotho", "Liberia", "Madagascar",
  "Malawi", "Mali", "Mauritania", "Mauritius", "Mozambique", "Namibia", "Niger",
  "Nigeria", "Rwanda", "Senegal", "Sierra Leone", "South Africa",
  "Togo", "Uganda",  "Zambia", "Zimbabwe", "United Republic of Tanzania", "World"
)
# Keep only the selected regions, then rename to World Bank / NCD-RisC style names so joins work.
old_data2 <- all_data %>%
  filter(Region %in% regions_to_keep)

old_data2$Region[old_data2$Region == "Congo"] <- "Congo, Rep."
old_data2$Region[old_data2$Region ==  "United Republic of Tanzania"] <- "Tanzania"
old_data2$Region[old_data2$Region ==  "Gambia"] <- "Gambia, The"
old_data2$Region[old_data2$Region ==  "Côte d'Ivoire"] <- "Cote d'Ivoire"

unique(old_data2$Region)
#######################
#Elements to keep
unique(old_data2$Element)

# Keep supply, trade and use elements. Only "Food supply quantity (kg/capita/yr)" and
# "Food supply (kcal/capita/day)" are used further down.
Elements_to_keep <- c(
  "Food supply quantity (kg/capita/yr)", "Food supply (kcal/capita/day)", "Export Quantity", "Production",
  "Import Quantity", "Processing", "Losses", "Feed", "Seed", "Other uses (non-food)"
)
data <- old_data2 %>%
  filter(Element %in% Elements_to_keep)

unique(data$Element)
#######################
#Items to keep
unique(data$Item)
unique(data$Item)

# Food items grouped into food groups later. Includes "Grand Total" (total energy supply).
items_to_keep <- c("Wheat and products", "Rice and products", "Barley and products", "Maize and products",
"Rye and products", "Oats", "Millet and products", "Sorghum and products",
"Cereals, other","Potatoes and products", "Cassava and products", "Sweet potatoes",
"Roots, Other", "Yams", "Starchy Roots", "Fish, Liver Oil", "Fish, Body Oil",
"Cream", "Butter, Ghee", "Fats, Animals, Raw", "Oilcrops Oil, Other", "Maize Germ Oil",
"Ricebran Oil", "Olive Oil", "Sesameseed Oil", "Coconut Oil", "Palm Oil", "Palmkernel Oil",
"Cottonseed Oil", "Rape and Mustard Oil",  "Sunflowerseed Oil", "Groundnut Oil", "Soyabean Oil",
"Bovine Meat", "Mutton & Goat Meat", "Pigmeat", "Poultry Meat", "Meat, Other", "Offals, Edible",
"Eggs","Freshwater Fish", "Demersal Fish", "Pelagic Fish","Marine Fish, Other","Animal fats",
"Crustaceans", "Cephalopods", "Molluscs, Other", "Aquatic Animals, Others",
"Milk - Excluding Butter","Beans", "Peas", "Pulses, Other and products", "Soyabeans",
"Nuts and products", "Groundnuts", "Sunflower seed", "Rape and Mustardseed", "Cottonseed",
"Coconuts - Incl Copra", "Sesame seed", "Palm kernels",
"Oilcrops, Other", "Cocoa Beans and products", "Tomatoes and products", "Onions",
"Vegetables, other", "Oranges,  Mandarines", "Lemons, Limes and products", "Grapefruit and products",
 "Citrus, Other", "Bananas", "Plantains", "Apples and products", "Pineapples and products",
"Dates", "Grapes and products (excl wine)",  "Fruits, other", "Pepper","Pimento",
"Oranges, Mandarines", "Cloves", "Sugar cane", "Sugar beet", "Sugar non-centrifugal",
"Sugar (Raw Equivalent)", "Honey", "Sweeteners, Other", "Grand Total"
)
data2 <- data %>%
  filter(Item %in% items_to_keep)
#######################
#convert to numeric
# Year and Value were text; as.numeric() turns any remaining non-numeric entries into NA (with a warning).
data2$Year<- as.numeric(data2$Year)
data2$Value<- as.numeric(data2$Value)

print(data2)
unique(data2$Item)
unique(data2$Item)
#######################
# Remove rows where Value is "X"
data2 <- data2 %>%
  filter(Value != "X")

print(data2)
#######################
#Filter the years 1990-2013
unique(data2$Year)

data2 <- data2 %>%
  filter(Year >= 1990 & Year <= 2013)

print(data2)
#######################
#select the Food supply quantity (kg/capita/yr)
# Keep food supply quantity only (kg per person per year).
supply_data2 <- data2 %>% filter(Element  == "Food supply quantity (kg/capita/yr)")
print(supply_data2)
#######################
#CONVERT from kg/capita/yr to grams/capita/day
supply_data2_grams <- supply_data2 %>%
# kg/capita/year -> g/capita/day (x1000 g, /365 days; leap years ignored).
  mutate(g_capita = (Value * 1000) / 365)   #creates a new column Value_g_per_day

print(supply_data2_grams)
#######################
#Combine food items into food groups
# Map each food item to a food group using case_when(); items not listed become NA.
group_supply <- supply_data2_grams %>%
  mutate(Food_Group = case_when(

# Cereals
    Item %in% c("Wheat and products", "Rice and products", "Barley and products",
                "Maize and products", "Rye and products", "Oats", "Millet and products",
                "Sorghum and products", "Cereals, other") ~ "Cereals",

 #roots
  Item %in% c("Potatoes and products", "Cassava and products", "Sweet potatoes",
              "Roots, Other", "Yams", "Starchy Roots") ~ "Roots",


 # Oils
    Item %in% c("Fish, Liver Oil", "Fish, Body Oil", "Cream", "Butter, Ghee",
                "Fats, Animals, Raw", "Oilcrops Oil, Other", "Maize Germ Oil",
                "Ricebran Oil", "Olive Oil", "Sesameseed Oil", "Coconut Oil",
                "Palm Oil", "Palmkernel Oil", "Cottonseed Oil", "Rape and Mustard Oil",
                "Sunflowerseed Oil", "Groundnut Oil", "Soyabean Oil", "Animal fats") ~ "Oils",

  # Animal products
    Item %in% c("Bovine Meat", "Mutton & Goat Meat", "Pigmeat", "Poultry Meat",
                "Meat, Other", "Offals, Edible") ~ "Meat and products",

# Eggs
    Item %in% c("Eggs") ~ "Eggs",


# Fish
    Item %in% c("Freshwater Fish", "Demersal Fish", "Pelagic Fish",
  "Marine Fish, Other", "Crustaceans", "Cephalopods", "Molluscs, Other",
  "Aquatic Animals, Others") ~ "Fish",


# Dairy
 Item %in% c("Milk - Excluding Butter") ~ "Dairy",

    # Pulses
 Item %in% c("Beans", "Peas", "Pulses, Other and products", "Soyabeans") ~ "Pulses",

     #Nuts and seeds
 Item %in% c("Nuts and products", "Groundnuts", "Groundnuts (Shelled Eq)", "Sunflower seed",
             "Rape and Mustardseed", "Cottonseed", "Coconuts - Incl Copra", "Sesame seed", "Palm kernels",
             "Oilcrops, Other", "Cocoa Beans and products") ~ "Nuts",


# Fruits and vegetables
    Item %in% c("Tomatoes and products", "Onions", "Vegetables, other", "Oranges,
                Mandarines", "Lemons, Limes and products", "Grapefruit and products",
                "Citrus, Other", "Bananas", "Plantains", "Apples and products",
                "Pineapples and products", "Dates", "Grapes and products (excl wine)",
                "Fruits, other", "Pepper","Pimento", "Oranges, Mandarines", "Cloves") ~ "Fruit and vegetables",

# Sweets and sugar
    Item %in% c("Sugar cane", "Sugar beet", "Sugar non-centrifugal", "Sugar (Raw Equivalent)",
                "Honey", "Sweeteners, Other") ~ "Sweets and sugar",

 #Grand Total
 Item %in% c("Grand Total") ~ "Total",

    TRUE ~ NA_character_    # To catch unmatched values
  ))


print(group_supply)
#######################
NA_items <- print(group_supply)   %>%
  filter(is.na(Food_Group)) %>%
  distinct(Item)

print(NA_items)
#######################
# Combine items into grouped categories using case_when
unique(group_supply$Food_Group)
# Food groups kept for the analysis ("Total" is excluded here).
food_groups <- c("Cereals", "Roots", "Fruit and vegetables", "Pulses", "Nuts",
                       "Meat and products", "Eggs", "Dairy", "Fish", "Sweets and sugar", "Oils")

# Filter and group
# Collapse into 8 analysis groups (meat, eggs, dairy and fish -> "Animal Sources") and
# sum g/capita/day per Region x Year x group. Result: food_suppl_old (1990-2013).
food_suppl_old <- group_supply %>%
  filter(!is.na(Food_Group), Food_Group %in% food_groups) %>%  # Keep only valid groups
  mutate(Grouped_Item = case_when(
    Food_Group == "Cereals" ~ "Cereals",
    Food_Group == "Roots" ~ "Starchy Roots",
    Food_Group == "Fruit and vegetables" ~ "Fruit and vegetables",
    Food_Group == "Pulses" ~ "Pulses",
     Food_Group == "Nuts" ~ "Nuts & seeds",
    Food_Group %in% c("Meat and products", "Eggs", "Dairy", "Fish") ~ "Animal Sources",
    Food_Group == "Sweets and sugar" ~ "Sweets and Sugar",
    Food_Group == "Oils" ~ "Oils",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_  # To catch unmatched values
  )) %>%
  group_by(Region, Year, Grouped_Item) %>%
  summarise(g_capita = sum(g_capita, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

print(food_suppl_old )
unique(food_suppl_old $Region)
unique(food_suppl_old $Grouped_Item)
```

# Merge and offset food supply data
```{r}
# Filter overlapping years
print(food_suppl_new)
print(food_suppl_old)

# ---- 2. HARMONISE THE TWO FAO RELEASES ----
# The releases overlap in 2010-2013. Values differ slightly because of revisions, so the old series
# is rescaled to the new release using the ratio of the overlap-year means. The result is one
# continuous 1990-2022 series (my_data).
old_overlap <- food_suppl_old %>% filter(Year >= 2010 & Year <= 2013)
new_overlap <- food_suppl_new %>% filter(Year >= 2010 & Year <= 2013)
print(old_overlap)
print(new_overlap)
#######################
# Create SSA average
# SSA average = simple (unweighted) mean over all countries except "World".
ssa_avg_overlap1 <- old_overlap %>%
  filter(!Region %in% c("World")) %>%
  group_by(Year, Grouped_Item) %>%
  summarise(value_old = mean(g_capita, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(Region = "SSA")

print(ssa_avg_overlap1)

ssa_avg_overlap2 <- new_overlap %>%
  filter(!Region %in% c("World")) %>%
  group_by(Year, Grouped_Item) %>%
  summarise(value_new = mean(g_capita_new, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(Region = "SSA")

print(ssa_avg_overlap2)
#######################
# Merge the overlapping datasets
merged_overlap <- ssa_avg_overlap1 %>%
  full_join(ssa_avg_overlap2, by = c("Region", "Year", "Grouped_Item"))
print(merged_overlap)
#######################
# Reshape for plotting
plot_data <- merged_overlap %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(value_new, value_old ),
               names_to = "Source",
               values_to = "g_capita_value")
print(plot_data)
#######################
# Plot
# Bar chart comparing old vs new release in the overlap years (visual check of the offset).
plot_overlap <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Grouped_Item, y = g_capita_value, fill = Source)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  facet_wrap(~ Year + Region, scales = "free_x") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Comparison of values of overlapping years between old and new FAO_FBS",
       x = "Food Group",
       y = "Grams/person/capita",
       fill = "Data Source") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 20, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 20),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 22),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 22),
     axis.title.y = element_text(size = 22),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 22),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 22, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 22),
        panel.spacing = unit(2, "cm"))

print(plot_overlap)


png(file.path(FIG_DIR, "Comparison.png"),
    width = 20, height = 18, units = "in", res = 1200)
grid.draw(plot_overlap)
dev.off()
#######################
# Join overlapping datasets
joined_overlap <- inner_join(old_overlap , new_overlap ,
                            by = c("Region", "Grouped_Item", "Year"))

print(joined_overlap)

#######################
# Calculate offset by region_item
# Offset = mean(new) / mean(old) over 2010-2013, per Region x food group.
offset_ratios <- joined_overlap %>%
  group_by(Region, Grouped_Item) %>%
  summarise(offset_ratio = mean(g_capita_new, na.rm = TRUE) / mean(g_capita, na.rm = TRUE))

offset_ratios
#######################
#apply offset ratio to newdatapre
# Rescale the old series by the offset (unchanged where no ratio is available).
old_adjusted <- food_suppl_old %>%
  left_join(offset_ratios, by = c("Region", "Grouped_Item")) %>%
  mutate(g_capita_adj = ifelse(!is.na(offset_ratio),
                         g_capita * offset_ratio,
                         g_capita))

print(old_adjusted)
#######################
# Keep only adjusted values
food_suppl_adj <- old_adjusted %>%
  select(Region, Year, Grouped_Item, g_adj_old = g_capita_adj)
#######################
#filter 2014_2022:
# Years after the overlap come straight from the new database.
data_2014_2022 <- food_suppl_new %>%
  filter(Year >= 2014, Year <= 2022)

print(data_2014_2022)
#######################
# Combine adjusted old and new data
# Stack adjusted old data (1990-2013) and new data (2014-2022).
my_data <- bind_rows(data_2014_2022, food_suppl_adj)
print(my_data)
unique(my_data$Year)
#######################
#Keep only one value
my_data <- my_data %>%
# Each row has either a new or an adjusted-old value; coalesce() merges them into one "value" column.
# Result: my_data = Region x Year x food group, g/capita/day, 1990-2022.
  mutate(value = coalesce(g_capita_new, g_adj_old)) %>%
  select(-g_capita_new, -g_adj_old)

print(my_data)
unique(my_data$Year)
```

```{r}
# Define items and countries of interest
# Food groups and regions shown in the stacked share chart.
items_selected <- c("Animal Sources", "Cereals", "Starchy Roots", "Fruit and vegetables", "Oils", "Pulses", "Nuts & seeds", "Sweets and Sugar")
countries_selected <- c("Kenya", "SSA", "World")
#######################
# Filter combined data for items and countries of interest
print(combined_supply )

food_supply_bar <- combined_supply  %>%
  filter(Grouped_Item %in% items_selected, Region %in% countries_selected) %>%
  mutate(Year = as.numeric(Year),  value = as.numeric( value)) %>%
  arrange(Region, Grouped_Item, Year)
#######################
# calculate percentages
# Share of each group (%) within Region x Year.
# NOTE: the denominator is the sum of the 8 selected groups only, not the total diet.
data_pct_grouped <- food_supply_bar %>%
  group_by(Region, Year) %>%
  mutate(Percent = ( value/ sum( value)) * 100) %>%
  ungroup()
#######################
#Arrange the food groups
data_pct_grouped$Grouped_Item <- factor(
  data_pct_grouped$Grouped_Item,
  levels = c(
   "Sweets and Sugar",
    "Oils",
    "Animal Sources",
    "Pulses",
    "Nuts & seeds",
    "Fruit and vegetables",
    "Starchy Roots",
    "Cereals"
  )
)
#######################
# Plot with grouped items
data_pct_grouped$Year <- factor(data_pct_grouped$Year, levels = sort(unique(data_pct_grouped$Year), decreasing = TRUE))


# Horizontal stacked bars, one panel per region; every 3rd year is labelled.
bar_graph_grouped <- ggplot(data_pct_grouped, aes(x = factor(Year), y = Percent, fill = Grouped_Item)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  coord_flip() + # Flip to horizontal bars
  facet_wrap(~ Region, nrow = 1) +  # Side-by-side facets
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
       "Sweets and Sugar" = "#cc3366",
       "Oils" = "#ff9900",
       "Pulses" = "sienna",
       "Nuts & seeds" =  "dodgerblue",
       "Animal Sources" = "gray76",
       "Fruit and vegetables" =  "springgreen4",
       "Starchy Roots" = "salmon1",
       "Cereals" = "#d9b38c"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 10)) +
  labs(
    title = "Share of food supply (g/person/day)",
    x = "",
    y = "Percent",
    fill = "Food Group"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 20),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 16),
       axis.text.x = element_text(size = 16),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 18),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 18),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "bottom",
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(breaks = function(x) x[seq(1, length(x), by = 3)])

print(bar_graph_grouped)
#######################
# Save the plots
png(file.path(FIG_DIR, "bar_graph1.png"),
    width = 18, height = 11, units = "in", res = 1400)
print(bar_graph_grouped)
dev.off()
```

# socioeconomic drivers data
```{r}

# ---- 4. SOCIOECONOMIC DRIVERS (World Bank-style indicators) ----
# Wide file: one column per year, named like "1990 [YR1990]".
Data <- read_excel(file.path(DATA_DIR, "drivers", "All countries.xlsx"))
print(Data)
#######################
#Check names and data structure
colnames(Data)
print(head(Data))
#######################
# Inspect the data for non-numeric values in year columns
# Check which year cells contain something other than digits/dots (e.g. ".." for missing).
year_columns <- Data %>% select(starts_with("19") | starts_with("20"))
non_numeric_values <- year_columns %>% filter_all(any_vars(!grepl("^[0-9.]+$", .)))
#######################
# Print non-numeric values if any
print(non_numeric_values)
#######################
# Convert all year columns to numeric
# Convert year columns to numeric by stripping non-numeric characters.
Data <- Data %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("19") | starts_with("20"), ~ as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.]", "", .))))
#######################
# Check for any remaining NAs after conversion
na_values <- Data %>% filter_all(any_vars(is.na(.)))
print(na_values)
#######################
#change to long format
# Wide -> long. (Lower-case "data" is a generic name; consider renaming to avoid confusion.)
data <- Data %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("19") | starts_with("20"), names_to = "Year", values_to = "Value")
print(data)
#######################
#Remove [YR xxx] from the Year columns
# "1990 [YR1990]" -> "1990".
data$Year <-gsub("\\s*\\[YR([0-9]+)\\]", "",data$Year)   #\\s*- Matches any white space (including the space before the bracket)
# \\[YR([0-9]    Matches the bracketed part [YR1990]

print(data)
#######################
data <- data %>%
  rename(Region = "Country Name",
         Element = "Series Name")

print(data)
#######################
# Remove unnecessary columns
```

# 2022 fsQCA
```{r}
#2022 data
colSums(is.na(fuzzy_AFR_2022))  #no Nas
#######################
#min, median and max
# ---- 9. fsQCA 2022 ----
# Step 1: inspect distributions (min / median / max) to choose calibration anchors.
summary(fuzzy_AFR_2022$Cereals)
summary(fuzzy_AFR_2022$`Fruit and vegetables`)
summary(fuzzy_AFR_2022$Pulses)
summary(fuzzy_AFR_2022$`Animal Sources`)
summary(fuzzy_AFR_2022$`Starchy Roots`)
summary(fuzzy_AFR_2022$`Nuts & seeds`)
summary(fuzzy_AFR_2022$`Sweets and Sugar`)
summary(fuzzy_AFR_2022$`Urban population`)
summary(fuzzy_AFR_2022$`female employment`)
summary(fuzzy_AFR_2022$`Employment in agriculture`)
summary(fuzzy_AFR_2022$BMI)
#######################
#Percentiles 10, 50, 90
# 10th / 50th / 90th percentiles, used as anchors for the "...90_22" conditions.
quantile(fuzzy_AFR_2022$`Employment in agriculture`,
         probs = c(.10, .50, .90),
         na.rm = TRUE)

quantile(fuzzy_AFR_2022$`female employment`,
         probs = c(.10, .50, .90),
         na.rm = TRUE)

quantile(fuzzy_AFR_2022$`Urban population`,
         probs = c(.10, .50, .90),
         na.rm = TRUE)

quantile(fuzzy_AFR_2022$`Arable land`,
         probs = c(.10, .50, .90),
         na.rm = TRUE)

quantile(fuzzy_AFR_2022$`Food imports`,
         probs = c(.10, .50, .90),
         na.rm = TRUE)
quantile(fuzzy_AFR_2022$BMI,
         probs = c(.10, .50, .90),
         na.rm = TRUE)
#######################
#Calibrate
# Step 2: direct fuzzy calibration with QCA::calibrate(). thresholds = c(full exclusion, crossover, full inclusion).
# Outcome BMI_22 = membership in "high obesity prevalence" (anchors = 10th/50th/90th percentile).
fuzzy_AFR_2022$BMI_22 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_2022$BMI, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(6.69, 11.91, 21.60))

#high-income   >$13854 or higher,
#upper-middle   $4466-$13845,
#lower-middle   $1136-$4465,
#low-income    <$1136 and less
# GNI anchors follow World Bank income thresholds (exclusion 4,466 / crossover 9,156 / inclusion 13,854 US$).
fuzzy_AFR_2022$GNI_22 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_2022$GNI, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(4466, 9156, 13854))

# Food-group conditions: anchors based on EAT-Lancet ranges (crossover = EAT-Lancet target).
fuzzy_AFR_2022$SS_22 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_2022$`Sweets and Sugar`, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(0.08, 31, 62))
fuzzy_AFR_2022$Cr_22 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_2022$Cereals, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(122.8, 232, 464))
fuzzy_AFR_2022$FV_22 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_2022$`Fruit and vegetables`, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(100, 300, 600))
fuzzy_AFR_2022$Pl_22 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_2022$Pulses, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(0.575, 75, 150))
fuzzy_AFR_2022$NS_22 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_2022$`Nuts & seeds`, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(0.301, 50, 100))
fuzzy_AFR_2022$An_22 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_2022$`Animal Sources`, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(82.05, 157, 334))
fuzzy_AFR_2022$Rt_22 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_2022$`Starchy Roots`, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(41.34, 50, 100))

#Median, mean,
# Alternative calibration (min / median / max) for the socioeconomic conditions. Not used in the QCA below.
fuzzy_AFR_2022$agric_22 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_2022$`Employment in agriculture`, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(5.47, 43.05, 70.70))
fuzzy_AFR_2022$Urban_22 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_2022$`Urban population`, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(16.89, 45.24, 90.73))
fuzzy_AFR_2022$female_22 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_2022$`female employment`, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(17.07, 46.66, 85.97))
fuzzy_AFR_2022$imports_22 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_2022$`Food imports`, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(6.38, 17.16, 30))
fuzzy_AFR_2022$land_22 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_2022$`Arable land`, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(0.44, 16.65, 51.41))
fuzzy_AFR_2022$GNI1_22 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_2022$GNI, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(4466, 9156, 13854))

#Percentiles
# Calibration used in the QCA: 10th / 50th / 90th percentile of each condition.
fuzzy_AFR_2022$Agric90_22 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_2022$`Employment in agriculture`, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(18.77, 41.48, 69.61))
fuzzy_AFR_2022$Fe90_22 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_2022$`female employment`, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(22.83, 44.94, 73.25))
fuzzy_AFR_2022$Urb90_22 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_2022$`Urban population`, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(23.64, 44.48, 68.16))
fuzzy_AFR_2022$Land90_22 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_2022$`Arable land`, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(1.51, 12.76, 41.08))
fuzzy_AFR_2022$Imports90_22 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_2022$`Food imports`, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(9.74, 17.42, 24.38))
#######################

# Summary to check distribution of calibrated BMI: its distribution should not be extremely skewed.
summary(fuzzy_AFR_2022$BMI_22)
# histogram to check distribution of calibrated BMI
hist(fuzzy_AFR_2022$BMI_22,
     main = "Fuzzy Set Membership: BMI",
     xlab = "Membership Score",
     col = "lightblue",
     border = "black")


#############################################################################################################################################################
#############################################################################################################################################################
#############################################################################################################################################################



#create data frame for conditions and outcome only
# Step 3: data frame with only the calibrated outcome and conditions (QCA needs a plain data.frame).
qca_data22 <- fuzzy_AFR_2022 %>%
  dplyr::select(
    BMI_22,
    Agric90_22,
    Land90_22,
    Urb90_22,
    Fe90_22,
    GNI_22,
    SS_22,
    Cr_22,
    FV_22,
    Pl_22,
    NS_22,
    An_22,
    Rt_22
  ) %>%
  as.data.frame()
#######################
#Necessity Analysis for presence of outcome
# Step 4: necessity analysis. A condition is necessary if consistency (inclN) is high
# (conventionally >= 0.90) and its relevance (RoN / covN) is not trivial.
necessity2_2022<- pof(data = qca_data22,
                     outcome = "BMI_22",
                     conditions = c(
                       "Agric90_22",
                       "Urb90_22",
                       "Fe90_22",
                       "Land90_22",
                       "GNI_22",
                       "SS_22",
                       "Cr_22",
                       "FV_22",
                       "Pl_22",
                       "NS_22",
                       "An_22",
                       "Rt_22"
                       ),
                       relation = "necessity")

print(necessity2_2022)

#######################
# Test necessity for absence of high obesity (outcome = 0)
# Negated outcome (membership in LOW obesity = 1 - membership in high obesity).
qca_data22$low_BMI_22 <- 1 - qca_data22$BMI_22

necessity_low <- pof(
  data = qca_data22,
  outcome = "low_BMI_22",
  conditions = c(
                       "Agric90_22",
                       "Urb90_22",
                       "Fe90_22",
                       "Land90_22",
                       "GNI_22",
                       "SS_22",
                       "Cr_22",
                       "FV_22",
                       "Pl_22",
                       "NS_22",
                       "An_22",
                       "Rt_22"),
  relation = "necessity")

print(necessity_low)

#######################
# Create a truth table 
# Step 5: truth table (sufficiency). Eight conditions are used 
# incl.cut = 0.8: minimum consistency for a row to count as sufficient; n.cut = 2: minimum cases per row;
# pri.cut = 0.7: minimum PRI to avoid rows that are also sufficient for the negated outcome.
#
tt_2022<- truthTable(data = qca_data22 ,
                 outcome = "BMI_22",
                 conditions = c(
                       "Agric90_22",
                       "Urb90_22",
                       "Fe90_22",
                       "GNI_22",
                       "SS_22",
                       "FV_22",
                       "Pl_22",
                       "An_22"
                       ),
                 incl.cut = 0.8,
                 pri.cut = 0.7,
                 n.cut = 2,
                complete =TRUE,
                show.cases = TRUE)

print(tt_2022)
#######################
#Complex Solution
# Step 6: Boolean minimisation. Complex solution = no counterfactuals (remainders excluded).
sol_2022 <- minimize(
  tt_2022,
  include = "?",
  details = TRUE,
  solution.type = "complex",
  show.cases = TRUE)

print(sol_2022)

#######################
# parsimonious solution
# Parsimonious solution = all remainders may be used as simplifying assumptions.
parsi_2022 <- minimize(
  tt_2022,
  include = "?",
  details = TRUE,
  show.cases = TRUE,
  solution.type = "parsimonious")

print(parsi_2022)
#######################
#Intermediate solution
# Intermediate solution = only "easy" counterfactuals consistent with directional expectations.
# 1 = presence of the condition is expected to contribute to high obesity; "-" = no expectation.
dir.exp1 <- c(                  # directional expectations
"-",  # Agric90_22             # A value of 1 suggests the theoretical expectation that the presence of the condition contributes to the outcome
 1,   # Urb90_22                # "-" suggests the theoretical expectation was not specified
 1,   # Fe90_22
 1,   # GNI_22
 1,   # SS_22
"-",  # FV_22
"-",  # Pl_22
"-"   # An_22
)

inter_2022 <- minimize(
  tt_2022,
  include = "?",
  details = TRUE,
  show.cases = TRUE,
  dir.exp = dir.exp1,
  solution.type = "intermediate"
)

print(inter_2022)
#######################
#To show the raw values and countries in the pathway
# Show raw data for the countries that appear in the solution paths.
cases1 <- c(3,9,14,24,27,33,5,15,31,1,6)
cases11 <-  fuzzy_AFR_2022[cases1, ]
print(cases11)

cases2 <- c(11,18,5,15,31)
cases12 <-  fuzzy_AFR_2022[cases2, ]
print(cases12)
View(cases12)

#######################
#Sufficiency analysis for low obesity
# Step 7: same procedure for the negated outcome (LOW obesity); QCA analyses are asymmetric.
ttlo_2022 <- truthTable(
  data = qca_data22,
  outcome = "low_BMI_22",
  conditions = c(
    "Agric90_22",
    "Urb90_22",
    "Fe90_22",
    "GNI_22",
    "SS_22",

  ),

  pri.cut = 0.7,
  n.cut = 2,
  complete = TRUE,

)

print(ttlo_2022)
#######################
#Complex Solution
sol_lo <- minimize(
  ttlo_2022,
  include = "?",
  details = TRUE,
  show.cases = TRUE,
  solution.type = "complex"
)
sol_lo
#######################
# parsimonious solution

                               include = "?",

#######################

)


linter_2022 <- minimize(
```

```{r}
# Calibration for 1992. Anchors differ from 2022 because the distributions differ
fuzzy_AFR_1992$BMI_92 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_1992$BMI, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(0.96, 2.5, 7.12))
fuzzy_AFR_1992$GNI1_92 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_1992$GNI, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(2695, 5526, 8355))

fuzzy_AFR_1992$SS_92 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_1992$`Sweets and Sugar`, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(2.4, 31, 62))
fuzzy_AFR_1992$Cr_92 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_1992$Cereals, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(82.36, 232, 464))
fuzzy_AFR_1992$FV_92 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_1992$`Fruit and vegetables`, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(100, 300, 600))
fuzzy_AFR_1992$Pl_92 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_1992$Pulses, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(0.48, 75, 150))
fuzzy_AFR_1992$NS_92 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_1992$`Nuts & seeds`, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(0.0, 50, 100))
fuzzy_AFR_1992$An_92 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_1992$`Animal Sources`, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(69.05, 157, 334))
fuzzy_AFR_1992$Rt_92 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_1992$`Starchy Roots`, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(25.73, 50, 100))

#Using percentiles
# Conditions calibrated with 10th / 50th / 90th percentiles.
fuzzy_AFR_1992$agric90_92 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_1992$`Employment in agriculture`, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(32.00, 58.64, 82.80))
fuzzy_AFR_1992$Urban90_92 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_1992$`Urban population`, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(13.97, 31.97, 48.42))
fuzzy_AFR_1992$female90_92 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_1992$`female employment`, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(11.31, 31.28, 50.11))
fuzzy_AFR_1992$land90_92 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_1992$`Arable land`, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(1.35, 10.05, 27.57))

#Using minimum, median, max
fuzzy_AFR_1992$agric_92 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_1992$`Employment in agriculture`, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(14.41, 58.62, 89.63))
fuzzy_AFR_1992$Urban_92 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_1992$`Urban population`, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(6.2, 32.02, 71.75))
fuzzy_AFR_1992$female_92 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_1992$`female employment`, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(6.24, 30.88, 69.65))
fuzzy_AFR_1992$imports_92 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_1992$`Food imports`, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(8.4, 13.47, 17.77))
#fuzzy_AFR_1992$land_92 <- calibrate(fuzzy_AFR_1992$`Arable land`, type = "fuzzy", thresholds = c(0.41, 11.77, 47.29))

#######################
#create data frame for conditions and outcome only
# Conditions + outcome only, as a data.frame.
qca_data92 <- fuzzy_AFR_1992 %>%
  dplyr::select(
    BMI_92,
    agric90_92,
    land90_92,
    Urban90_92,
    female90_92,
    GNI1_92,
    SS_92,
    Cr_92,
    FV_92,
    Pl_92,
    NS_92,
    An_92,
    Rt_92
  ) %>%
  as.data.frame()
#######################
#Necessity Analysis
# Necessity analysis (high obesity).
nec_1992<- pof(data = qca_data92,
                      outcome = "BMI_92",
                      conditions = c(
                        "agric90_92",
                        "Urban90_92",
                        "female90_92",
                        "land90_92",
                        "GNI1_92",
                        "SS_92",
                        "Cr_92",
                        "FV_92",
                        "Pl_92",
                        "NS_92",
                        "An_92",
                        "Rt_92"),
                      relation = "necessity")

print(nec_1992)
#######################
# Test necessity for absence of high obesity (outcome = 0)
qca_data92$low_BMI_92 <- 1 - qca_data92$BMI_92

# Necessity analysis for LOW obesity.

nec92_low <- pofind(
  data = qca_data92,
  outcome = "low_BMI_92",
  conditions = c(
    "agric90_92",
    "land90_92",
    "Urban90_92",
    "female90_92",
    "GNI1_92",
    "SS_92",
    "Cr_92",
    "FV_92",
    "Pl_92",
    "NS_92",
    "An_92",
    "Rt_92"),
  relation = "necessity"
)

print(nec92_low)
#######################
# Create a truth table
# Truth table, same cut-offs as for 2022 (incl.cut 0.80, n.cut 2, pri.cut 0.7).
tt_1992 <- truthTable(
  qca_data92,
  outcome = "BMI_92",
  conditions = c(
    agric90_92,
    Urban90_92,
    female90_92,
    GNI1_92,
    SS_92,
    FV_92,
    Pl_92,
    An_92
  ),
  incl.cut = 0.80,
  n.cut = 2,
  pri.cut = 0.7,
  show.cases = TRUE,
  complete =TRUE,
)

tt_1992
#######################
#Complex Solution
# Complex, parsimonious and intermediate solutions for high obesity in 1992.
sol_1992 <- minimize(
  tt_1992,
  include = "?",
  details = TRUE,
)
sol_1992
#######################
# parsimonious solution
pars_1992 <- minimize(tt_1992,
                       include = "?",
                       details = TRUE,
                       show.cases = TRUE,
                       dir.exp = NULL,
                       solution.type = "parsimonious")
print(pars_1992)
#######################
#Intermediate solution
# Directional expectations (1 = presence expected to contribute to high obesity; "-" = none).
dir.exph92 <- c(
  "-",   # agric90_92
   1,   # Urban90_92
   1,   # female90_92
   1,   # GNI1_92
  1,  # SS_92
  "-",  # FV_92
  "-",  # Pl_92
  "-"   # An_92
)

intermediate_1992 <- minimize(
 tt_1992,
  include = "?",
  details = TRUE,
  show.cases = TRUE,
  dir.exp = dir.exph92,
  solution.type = "intermediate"
)

print(intermediate_1992)
```
